subfield: Condensed matter and materials physics / photovoltaics
motivation: I nominate Tsutomu Miyasaka, Nam-Gyu Park and Henry Snaith for discovering and establishing metal-halide perovskite solar cells. Miyasaka first used organometal halide perovskites as photovoltaic absorbers in 2009. Park made the first stable solid-state perovskite device, with about 9% efficiency, in 2012. Snaith showed the same year that perovskites carry charge by themselves in meso-superstructured and planar thin-film cells. That result revealed the materials' remarkable physics: long carrier diffusion lengths, high defect tolerance, sharp absorption edges and tunable bandgaps. In little more than a decade, solution-processed perovskites have gone from about 4% to over 26% single-junction efficiency, and perovskite–silicon tandems now exceed 34%. This is one of the fastest advances in the history of semiconductor physics. The work opened a new field that spans condensed-matter physics, chemistry and engineering, and it has moved into industrial tandem modules, with major consequences for the global energy transition.
